problem: The diagram sends ker T to '0 in W' and sends 'other inputs' to 'range T'. Read as drawn, it says the range is built only from the non-kernel inputs and that 0 is outside the range. In fact T(ker T) = {0} is inside im T, so im T contains 0 and is the span of all images, kernel images included.
fix: Add an edge from the '0 in W' block into the 'range T' block (or put 0 inside the range block) and label it 'range T (contains 0)'. Keep the aria sentence: 'the images of the remaining inputs lie in the range, which also contains 0'.

problem: 'Drop it if a free-variable solution produces it' describes a case that cannot happen. In the free-variable method each free parameter equals 1 in its own coordinate of its coefficient vector, so that vector is never the zero vector. A student may waste time looking for a zero vector that is not there.
fix: Say: 'A basis never contains the zero vector. The free-variable vectors are automatically nonzero, so the real check is that they are independent and that none is a combination of the others.'

problem: The answer writes T(v) = 0 without saying which zero. Here V and W are different spaces, so the zero on the right is the zero vector of W, not of V. The formula in Section 1 defines this; the quiz answer should repeat it.
fix: ker T = {v ∈ V : T(v) = 0_W}, where 0_W is the zero vector of W; im T = {T(v) : v ∈ V}.
